title: Shifted generators detect isomorphisms on their localizing closure
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a locally small triangulated category with all small coproducts [def-weil-triangulated-category]. Fix a class $\mathcal S$ of objects. Define $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal S)$ to be the intersection of the full replete triangulated subcategories [def-weil-triangulated-subcategory] containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under all small coproducts. Let $\alpha:B\to G$ be a morphism with $B,G\in\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal S)$. If postcomposition with $\alpha$ gives bijections $\operatorname{Hom}(S[n],B)\to\operatorname{Hom}(S[n],G)$ for all $S\in\mathcal S$ and $n\in\mathbf Z$, then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism. Neither compactness nor smallness of the class $\mathcal S$ is assumed; coproducts and Hom sets use one fixed universe.

source.place: Closed-adjoint uniqueness and final restriction paragraphs: localizing generator test

proof.text: By TR1 choose a distinguished triangle $B\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\xrightarrow{p}C\xrightarrow{\delta}B[1]$. In every full replete triangulated subcategory containing $\mathcal S$ and closed under small coproducts, both $B$ and $G$ belong by the hypotheses. Rotating this triangle and using extension closure shows that $C$ belongs too. Thus $C\in\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal S)$.

Fix $S\in\mathcal S$, $n\in\mathbf Z$, and put $W=S[n]$. The hypothesis also implies injectivity of $\operatorname{Hom}(W,B[1])\xrightarrow{\alpha[1]\circ-}\operatorname{Hom}(W,G[1])$: applying the inverse shift identifies this map with postcomposition by $\alpha$ on maps out of $S[n-1]$. For $f:W\to C$, consecutive composites in the triangle give $\alpha[1]\delta f=0$, so injectivity gives $\delta f=0$. Exactness at $\operatorname{Hom}(W,C)$, obtained by applying clause (ii) of the cited Hom-exactness node to the rotated triangle, yields $g:W\to G$ with $f=pg$. Surjectivity in the hypothesis gives $h:W\to B$ with $g=\alpha h$. Hence $f=p\alpha h=0$. Therefore every map $S[n]\to C$ vanishes.

source.place: Tags 0146, lemma-composition-zero, and 0149, lemma-representable-homological; the exact-sequence argument of lemma-pre-prepare-adjoint

proof.text: Let $\mathcal Q$ be the replete class of all shifts $C[m]$ for $m\in\mathbf Z$. It is stable under shifts because $(C[m])[r]\cong C[m+r]$. By the left-orthogonal lemma, the full subcategory $\mathcal O={}^{\perp}\mathcal Q$ is replete and triangulated. It is also closed under every small coproduct: if $X_i\in\mathcal O$ and $u:\coprod_iX_i\to Q$ with $Q\in\mathcal Q$, then $u\iota_i=0$ for each coproduct injection $\iota_i$; uniqueness in the coproduct universal property forces $u=0$, also for the empty family. Thus $\mathcal O$ is one of the localizing subcategories used in the defining intersection as soon as it contains $\mathcal S$.

source.place: Tag 0FXC, lemma-orthogonal-triangulated; coproduct universal property (written out)

proof.text: For $S\in\mathcal S$ and $m\in\mathbf Z$, applying the inverse shift identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(S,C[m])$ with $\operatorname{Hom}(S[-m],C)$, which is zero by step 2. Isomorphisms to shifts of $C$ preserve this vanishing, so $\mathcal S\subseteq\mathcal O$. By the defining intersection, $\operatorname{Loc}(\mathcal S)\subseteq\mathcal O$. Step 1 now gives $C\in\mathcal O$, and $C=C[0]$ up to the shift-zero isomorphism belongs to $\mathcal Q$. Consequently $1_C=0$. Every map into $C$ equals $1_C$ composed with that map and is zero, and every map out of $C$ equals that map composed with $1_C$ and is zero. Since zero maps exist, $C$ is both initial and terminal, hence a zero object. This uses only individual objects of $\mathcal S$, never a coproduct indexed by $\mathcal S$.

proof.text: Apply the zero-cone criterion to the distinguished triangle $B\xrightarrow{\alpha}G\to C\to B[1]$ of step 1. Its third vertex is a zero object by step 4, so its first arrow $\alpha$ is an isomorphism.
